name: cisa-scuba
title: CISA SCuBA baselines for Microsoft 365
notice: Policy ids and statements are from CISA's Secure Cloud Business Applications baselines, published with ScubaGear and dedicated to the public domain (CC0 1.0).

items.MS.AAD.2.1v1: Users detected as high risk SHALL be blocked.
items.MS.AAD.2.2v1: A notification SHOULD be sent to the administrator when high-risk users are detected.
items.MS.AAD.2.3v1: Sign-ins detected as high-risk SHALL be blocked.
items.MS.AAD.3.1v1: Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be enforced for all users.
items.MS.AAD.3.2v2: MFA SHALL be enforced for all users.
items.MS.AAD.3.3v2: If Microsoft Authenticator is enabled, it SHALL be configured to show login context information.
items.MS.AAD.3.4v1: The "Authentication methods manage migration" feature SHALL be set to "Migration complete."
items.MS.AAD.3.5v2: The authentication methods of short message service (SMS), voice call, and email one-time passcode (OTP) SHALL be disabled.
items.MS.AAD.3.6v1: Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be required for highly privileged roles.
items.MS.AAD.3.7v1: Managed devices SHOULD be required for authentication.
items.MS.AAD.3.8v1: Managed devices SHOULD be required to register MFA.
items.MS.AAD.3.9v1: Device code authentication SHOULD be blocked.
items.MS.AAD.4.1v1: Security logs SHALL be sent to the agency's security operations center for monitoring.
items.MS.AAD.5.1v1: Only administrators SHALL be allowed to register applications.
items.MS.AAD.5.2v1: User consent to applications SHALL be restricted.
items.MS.AAD.5.3v1: An administrative consent workflow SHALL be configured for applications.
items.MS.AAD.5.5v1: Application password addition SHOULD be blocked.
items.MS.AAD.5.6v1: Application password lifetime SHOULD be restricted to 180 days or less.
items.MS.AAD.5.7v1: Application certificate lifetime SHOULD be restricted to 365 days or less.
items.MS.AAD.7.1v1: A minimum of two users and a maximum of eight users SHALL be provisioned with the Global Administrator role.
items.MS.AAD.7.2v1: Privileged users SHALL be provisioned with finer-grained roles instead of the Global Administrator role.
items.MS.AAD.7.3v1: Privileged users SHALL be provisioned cloud-only accounts separate from an on-premises directory or other federated identity providers.
items.MS.AAD.7.4v1: Permanent active role assignments SHALL NOT be allowed for highly privileged roles.
items.MS.AAD.7.5v1: Provisioning users to highly privileged roles SHALL NOT occur outside of a PAM system.
items.MS.AAD.7.6v1: Activation of the Global Administrator role SHALL require approval.
items.MS.AAD.7.7v1: Eligible and active highly privileged role assignments SHALL trigger an alert.
items.MS.AAD.7.8v1: User activation of the Global Administrator role SHALL trigger an alert.
items.MS.AAD.7.9v1: User activation of other highly privileged roles SHOULD trigger an alert.
items.MS.AAD.8.1v1: Guest users SHOULD have limited or restricted access to Microsoft Entra ID directory objects.
items.MS.AAD.8.2v1: Only users with the "Guest Inviter" role SHOULD be able to invite guest users.
items.MS.AAD.8.3v1: Guest invites SHOULD only be allowed to be sent to specific external domains that have been authorized by the agency for legitimate business purposes.
items.MS.AAD.9.1v1: Risky AI agents SHALL be blocked.
items.MS.EXO.1.1v2: Automatic forwarding to external domains SHALL be disabled.
items.MS.EXO.2.2v3: An SPF policy SHALL be published for each domain that fails all non-approved senders.
items.MS.EXO.3.1v1: DKIM SHOULD be enabled for all domains.
items.MS.EXO.4.1v1: A DMARC policy SHALL be published for every second-level domain.
items.MS.EXO.4.2v1: The DMARC message rejection option SHALL be p=reject.
items.MS.EXO.4.3v1: The DMARC point of contact for aggregate reports SHALL include the mailbox CISA names.
items.MS.EXO.4.4v1: An agency point of contact SHOULD be included for aggregate and failure reports.
items.MS.EXO.6.1v1: Contact folders SHALL NOT be shared with all domains.
items.MS.EXO.6.2v1: Calendar details SHALL NOT be shared with all domains.
items.MS.EXO.7.1v1: External sender warnings SHALL be implemented.
items.MS.POWERBI.1.1v1: The "Publish to Web" feature SHOULD be disabled unless the agency mission requires the capability.
items.MS.POWERBI.2.1v1: Guest user access to the Power BI tenant SHOULD be disabled unless the agency mission requires the capability.
items.MS.POWERBI.3.1v1: The "Invite external users to your organization" feature SHOULD be disabled unless agency mission requires the capability.
items.MS.POWERBI.4.1v1: Service principals with access to APIs SHOULD be restricted to specific security groups.
items.MS.POWERBI.4.2v1: Service principals' ability to create and use profiles SHOULD be restricted to specific security groups.
items.MS.POWERBI.5.1v1: ResourceKey-based authentication SHOULD be blocked unless a specific use case (e.g., streaming and/or "push" datasets) merits its use.
items.MS.POWERBI.6.1v1: Python and R interactions SHOULD be disabled.
items.MS.POWERBI.7.1v1: Sensitivity labels SHOULD be enabled for Power BI and employed for sensitive data per enterprise data protection policies.
items.MS.POWERPLATFORM.1.1v1: The ability to create production and sandbox environments SHALL be restricted to administrators.
items.MS.POWERPLATFORM.1.2v1: The ability to create trial environments SHALL be restricted to administrators.
items.MS.POWERPLATFORM.2.1v1: A DLP policy SHALL be created to restrict connector access in the default Power Platform environment.
items.MS.POWERPLATFORM.2.2v1: Non-default environments SHOULD have at least one DLP policy.
items.MS.POWERPLATFORM.3.1v1: Power Platform tenant isolation SHALL be enabled.
items.MS.POWERPLATFORM.3.2v1: An inbound/outbound connection allowlist SHOULD be configured.
items.MS.POWERPLATFORM.4.1v1: Content Security Policy (CSP) SHALL be enforced for model-driven and canvas Power Apps.
items.MS.POWERPLATFORM.5.1v1: The ability to create Power Pages sites SHOULD be restricted to administrators.
items.MS.POWERPLATFORM.6.1v1: The "Share with everyone" feature SHOULD be disabled.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.1v1: Emails with click-to-run file attachments SHALL be blocked including, at a minimum, .exe, .cmd, and .vbe files.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.2v1: Email scanning SHALL be capable of reviewing emails after delivery.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.3v1: Emails identified as containing malware SHALL be quarantined or dropped.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.4v1: SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams message attachments SHOULD be scanned for malware.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.2.1v1: User impersonation protection SHOULD be enabled for sensitive accounts.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.2.2v1: Domain impersonation protection SHOULD be enabled for domains owned by the agency.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.2.3v1: Domain impersonation protection SHOULD be added for key suppliers and partners.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.2.4v1: User warnings, comparable to the user safety tips included with EOP, SHOULD be displayed.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.1v1: A DLP policy SHALL be configured to protect PII and sensitive information, as defined by the agency, blocking at a minimum: credit card numbers, U.S. Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers (ITIN), and U.S. Social Security numbers (SSN).
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.2v1: The DLP policy SHOULD be applied to Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams chat, and Devices.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.3v1: The action for the DLP policy SHOULD be set to block sharing sensitive information with everyone.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.4v1: Notifications to inform users and help educate them on the proper use of sensitive information SHOULD be enabled in the DLP policy.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.5v1: The DLP policy SHOULD include an action to block access to sensitive information by restricted applications
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.4.1v1: At a minimum, the following alerts SHALL be enabled:
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.4.2v1: The alerts SHOULD be sent to a monitored address or incorporated into a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM).
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.5.1v1: Unified audit logging SHALL be enabled.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.5.2v1: Audit logs SHALL be retained and searchable for a minimum of 3 months and retrievable for a minimum of 12 months.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.6.1v1: Emails detected as spam and phishing SHALL NOT be delivered to the user's inbox.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.6.2v1: Allowed domains SHALL NOT be added to inbound anti-spam protection policies.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.7.1v1: URL comparison with a block-list SHOULD be enabled for URLs in emails, Teams messages, and Office documents.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.7.2v1: Direct download links SHOULD be scanned for malware.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.7.3v1: User click tracking SHOULD be enabled.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.8.1v1: IP allow lists SHOULD NOT be created.
items.MS.SECURITYSUITE.8.2v1: Safe lists SHOULD NOT be enabled.
items.MS.SHAREPOINT.1.1v1: External sharing for SharePoint SHALL be limited to "Existing guests" or "Only people in your organization."
items.MS.SHAREPOINT.1.2v1: External sharing for OneDrive SHALL be limited to "Existing guests" or "Only people in your organization."
items.MS.SHAREPOINT.1.3v1: External sharing SHALL be restricted to approved external domains and/or users in approved security groups per interagency collaboration needs.
items.MS.SHAREPOINT.2.1v1: File and folder default sharing scope SHALL be set to "Specific people (only the people the user specifies)."
items.MS.SHAREPOINT.2.2v1: File and folder default sharing permissions SHALL be set to view only.
items.MS.SHAREPOINT.3.1v1: Expiration days for "Anyone" links SHALL be set to 30 days or less.
items.MS.SHAREPOINT.3.2v1: The allowable file and folder permissions for links SHALL be set to view only.
items.MS.SHAREPOINT.3.3v2: Reauthentication days for people who use a verification code SHALL be set to 30 days or less.
items.MS.TEAMS.1.1v1: External meeting participants SHOULD NOT be enabled to request control of shared desktops or windows.
items.MS.TEAMS.1.2v2: Anonymous users SHALL NOT be enabled to start Microsoft Teams meetings.
items.MS.TEAMS.1.3v1: Anonymous users and dial-in callers SHOULD NOT be admitted automatically.
items.MS.TEAMS.1.4v1: Internal users SHOULD be admitted to Microsoft Teams meetings automatically.
items.MS.TEAMS.1.5v1: Dial-in users SHOULD NOT be enabled to bypass the lobby.
items.MS.TEAMS.1.7v2: "Record an event" SHOULD NOT be set to "Always record."
items.MS.TEAMS.2.1v2: External access for users SHALL only be enabled on a per-domain basis.
items.MS.TEAMS.2.2v2: Unmanaged users SHALL NOT be enabled to initiate contact with internal users.
items.MS.TEAMS.2.3v2: Internal users SHOULD NOT be enabled to initiate contact with unmanaged users.
items.MS.TEAMS.4.1v1: Microsoft Teams email integration SHALL be disabled.
items.MS.TEAMS.5.1v2: Agencies SHOULD only allow installation of Microsoft applications approved by the agency.
items.MS.TEAMS.5.2v2: Agencies SHOULD only allow installation of third-party applications approved by the agency.
items.MS.TEAMS.5.3v2: Agencies SHOULD only allow installation of custom applications approved by the agency.
